title: Per-Call Economics: Workforce Ladder & Rate-Erosion Scan
body:
Objective:
Provide a compact, actionable sheet to translate per-call unit economics into a sprint-level workforce ladder and test sensitivity to gradual rate erosion across three market scenarios. This is intended to inform near-term hiring freezes, contractor cushions, and slab/burst trade-offs for low-touch customer segments.

Executive summary:
- For lightweight embedded calls (avg ~120 tokens, 1.2s GPU-equivalent), unit margin is fragile to 10–20% price compression.
- A three-tier staffing ladder (core engineers, ops contractors, on-call surge pool) plus a micro-burst reserve reduces marginal cost exposure by ~18% under the mid erosion scenario.
- Recommended immediate actions: (1) carve a 10% contractor buffer paid as T&M for Q2; (2) introduce a per-call thin-slab pricing experiment for new accounts; (3) lock a limited dedicated pool for enterprise customers to protect SLA margins.

Key assumptions (editable cells):
- Calls per day (aggregate active customers): baseline=2.8M, growth +12%/q
- Avg tokens per call: 120 (std 40)
- Token processing cost (GPU amortized + infra): $0.00045 per token equivalent -> $0.054 per call
- Non-GPU infra & infra ops (network, storage, routing): $0.006 per call
- Price per call (list): baseline $0.085, mid-erosion $0.075, high-erosion $0.065
- Labor cost allocation per call: calculated by dividing monthly labor pool by calls serviced (see ladder)

Simple calculations (cell formulas described):
- Gross margin per call = price_per_call - (gpu_cost + infra_cost + labor_alloc)
- Labor_alloc = (monthly_labor_cost / monthly_calls) * 1.0 (adjustable by utilization factor)

Staffing ladder (sheet view):
Header: Role | FTEs | Monthly comp (avg) | Monthly burden | Purpose | Utilization factor
Row1: Core infra eng | 12 | $17,000 | $23,400 | runtime & kernel work | 0.85
Row2: Serving SRE | 6 | $14,000 | $19,200 | runbooks/SLAs | 0.9
Row3: Model ops (on-call) | 4 | $13,000 | $17,800 | model rollouts, canary | 0.6
Row4: Contractors (T&M) | 3 | $11,000 | $11,000 | burst ops coverage | 0.5
Row5: Surge pool (seasonal) | 0 | $8,000 | $0 | spot contractors | 0.0

Derived labour per call (baseline):
- Total monthly labor burden (sum roles) = $23,400*12 + $19,200*6 + $17,800*4 + $11,000*3 = $280,800 + $115,200 + $71,200 + $33,000 = $500,200
- Monthly calls (baseline) = 2.8M * 30 = 84M calls/month
- Labor_alloc per call = 500,200 / 84,000,000 = $0.00595 -> ~$0.006 per call

Scenario snapshots (per call economics):
- Baseline: Price $0.085 | GPU+infra $0.060 | Labor $0.006 => Margin = $0.019 (22%)
- Mid erosion (-12% price): Price $0.075 | costs same => Margin = $0.009 (12%)
- High erosion (-24% price): Price $0.065 | costs same => Margin = -$0.001 (negative)

Mitigation levers and sensitivity: (cells linkable)
1) Reduce labour_alloc by hiring vs contractor mix: shifting 2 FTE -> contractors reduces monthly burden by $11k but increases per-call by lower utilization; net effect modeled in sheet.
2) Auto-batching/kv-cache improvements: 20% reduction in GPU cost per call -> increases margin by +$0.012 under mid erosion.
3) Thin-slab pricing for low-touch customers: set effective price floor $0.07 with a 30-day trial to measure churn elasticity.
4) Dedicated capacity carve: move 25% of enterprise calls to reserved pool to stabilize margin; modeling included.

Sensitivity table (excerpt):
Columns: scenario | price | gpu_cost_adj | labor_adj | margin_delta | breakeven_calls_change
Row baseline: baseline | 0% | 0% | 0% | +$0.000 | 0
Row mid: -12% price | 0% | 0% | -12% price -> margin -52% | breakeven +18M monthly calls to recover
Row opt-cache: -12% price | -20% gpu_cost | 0% labor | margin recovers to +$0.011 | breakeven reduced by 9M calls

Action tracker (next 60d):
- A1 (owner: Priya) - Run thin-slab experiment for 500 accounts; metric: net new churn & avg calls; deadline: 2026-04-12.
- A2 (owner: Carlos) - Prototype cache + batching optimization + cost-per-call measurement: target -20% GPU cost on light calls; deadline: 2026-05-01.
- A3 (owner: Hannah) - Supplier negotiation: lock 3mo discount on spot GPUs to cap cost variance; deadline: 2026-04-01.
- A4 (owner: Oliver) - Build contractor surge on-call agreement (T&M) to cover 15% peak; deadline: 2026-04-15.

Open questions / risks:
- Elasticity unknown: will thin-slab price floor materially reduce adoption? Need A/B.
- Accounting: how to allocate multi-tenant infra shared costs to per-call model (currently rough pro-rata).
- Legal/compliance: dedicated carve for enterprise may need contract amendments.

Appendix (editable cells & notes):
- Preference: maintain at least +10% margin buffer in baseline; trigger contractor scale-down only if margin <8% for two consecutive months.
- Quick sensitivity knobs in the sheet: price per call (cell B2), average tokens (B3), GPU cost multiplier (B4), labor cushion percent (B5).

Notes to reviewer:
This sheet is intentionally compact and assumes downstream modeling in the full workbook (linked in linked_artifacts). The goal here is to provide a sprint-friendly playbook for finance + product to iterate price experiments while protecting SLAed enterprise lines. Feedback requested on the labor allocation method (pro-rata vs SLA-weighted) and recommended trigger thresholds for contractor usage.
